title: Towards Scalable Network-Based Interventions for HIV Treatment and Prevention via R2C-Agent
abstract: arXiv:2611.13312v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) remains a pressing public health challenge worldwide. Targeting limited HIV prevention and treatment resources effectively with network-based algorithms is a long-standing problem with a rich history at AAMAS and other computational venues. However, optimizing targeted biomedical interventions for minimizing spread of HIV often requires observability of the contact network of HIV transmission risk behavior among individuals, which is prohibitively expensive to collect at scale. Peer referral networks, i.e., networks collected through a recursive peer referral process, are an alternative network class often used to study HIV in hidden populations that can be collected digitally at scale, but they deviate from the underlying contact network: referrals can follow non-risk social ties and participants accept only one referral, hiding contacts among already-recruited individuals. translated_title: 基于R2C-Agent实现可扩展的网络化HIV治疗与预防干预
translated_abstract: 人类免疫缺陷病毒（HIV）仍然是全球范围内亟待解决的公共卫生挑战。如何利用基于网络的算法有效配置有限的HIV预防和治疗资源，是一个长期存在的研究问题，在AAMAS及其他计算领域的学术会议上有着丰富的研究历史。然而，为最小化HIV传播而优化针对性的生物医学干预措施，通常需要对个体之间HIV传播风险行为的接触网络进行观测，而大规模收集这类数据的成本高得令人望而却步。同伴推荐网络，即通过递归同伴推荐过程收集的网络，是另一类常用于研究隐性人群中HIV问题的网络，可以大规模地进行数字化收集，但其与底层接触网络存在偏差：推荐可能沿着无风险的社会关系进行，且参与者仅接受一次推荐，从而隐藏了已被招募个体之间的联系。在这项工作中，我们首先……
tldr: 该论文针对接触网络难以大规模获取的问题，提出利用R2C-Agent方法，基于可大规模数字化收集的同伴推荐网络开发可扩展的HIV治疗与预防干预策略。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the R2C-Agent approach to enable scalable network-based HIV treatment and prevention interventions by leveraging digitally collectable peer referral networks in place of prohibitively expensive contact networks.
